entries.speaker: D
entries.text: In the morning, we went to Peshawar Museum, there were lots of Buddah things there. Then we went and walked round a few streets, we bought some ‘Tikkas’, which were like Hamburgers, but VERY hot and spicy. We saw lots of shops selling gun holsters etc.. After lunch, Mum, Dad & I went for a walk together. We went to a perfume store, the man put lots of different kinds of perfume on my hand, they were super. I got Helena some Rose perfume in a tiny bottle, it cost 2 rupees (14p).

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to the Peshawar Museum. It had some nice tribal things including two huge arrow-spears that had a convex metal thing on the end (pic). Then we went to a bazaar and got some really spicy meatballs.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 37594 (9994 miles travelled). Peshawar

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: In the morning, Mum, Dad & I went to the Bazaar, Colin had a terrible sore through, so he stayed in bed. We saw lots of tin and copper shops, and in one area lots of shops with big straw baskets full of crushed, dried leaves, it was all tobacco, in the same area, there were lots of big oven, roasting nuts. In the afternoon, H & I bought handkerchief together (was one that we saw yesterday) (pic), it was black with a silver tree on it, and a bird in the tree, he put our names on it for us.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: There are some lovely birds of prey flying round the hotel, some with wing-spans about two yards. I would like a small bird of prey but it could not live in Australia. The girls bought a handkerchief.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove to ‘Dana’, it was a tribal area, all the shops, other than food and medicinal shops, made and/or sold guns, we had an interesting time with Colin, who knows lots about guns. Two shops sold ‘Hashish’. We got back to Peshawar and said goodby to Colin. Then we set out again. At the town where the Kabul River joined, The Indus, we camped at a ‘tourist Inn’, lovely pools flowing into each other, and at last down into the River.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We have been to a gun market. When we got to the village a man took us and showed us around. There were some nice rifles: they were heavier than I expected. What I liked was a small 0.22 automatic pistol. There were some really big bullets. All of the guns were made in small shops with primitive tools, not in big factories.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: Dak Bungalows. After visiting Darra which has lots of little shops which make and sell all kinds of guns, pistols etc we drove back to Peshawar and left Colin there. Then we drove off towards Taxila. We followed the Kabul river to where it joined the Indus. F and I went down to the Indus and found lots of super pools and sand. One pool we liked a lot.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 37739 (10139 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: There were lovely old trees all along the road, we saw lots of buffalo (enormous) pulling carts, and quite a few camels. We saw a sign to ‘Wah Gardens’ there were lots of beautiful tents up in the garden, we asked a Policeman what was happening and he said that Prime Minister was coming, so would we please go! Crikey! We drove on and after a bit of muddle, found the road to Taxila, and at the end of it, Taxila. We decided to sleep at the Resthouse, first we looked at the museum, and then at ?? monasteries, and Stuppes, which are smallish kind of memorials, intricately carved.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We were going to Taxila when we saw a sign to the mogul gardens. We decided to go, there were lots of people so we decided to go on a bit, but we found it only led to a village. So we came back and asked a policeman if we could go in. He said no because the PM was coming. When we were going, seven trucks of soldiers came by. We went on to Taxila. It had a good museum. I liked the water distiller best (pic). It was a bit like the glass one in a science lab but made of pottery. I think it was quite clever. It was earlier than 500 AD.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: On the way to Taxila, we stopped at the Wah Gardens. We were not allowed inside because the Prime Minister was coming that day. There were lots of brightly coloured tents on the lawns. At Taxila, we went to the Museum where there were lots of Buddhist statues. F and I liked better the ancient toys, beads and a pottery water distiller. (Pic)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We went to see some more ruins, the first had very smooth rounded walls, we found some small snake skins, then Dad found one that was over 5 feet long! After that, Mum and I were a bit nervous of all the rustlings in the grass.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We also saw a huge ruined city, unfortunately, most of it was only a bit above ground level. We bought a big bunch of bananas, and stopped for lunch, just out of Taxila, then we drove on to Raul-Pindi. At Raul-Pindi we visited the Army Museum, it had some quite interesting things there, from places we’ve been, or are going to. Then we drove the few km to Islamabad, and who did we see on the road? Colin! Off to stay with his rich friends. At the camping were Ian and Viv!

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to some more ruins. The wall was curved [PIC 1] and instead of ordinary brickwork the wall had big rough stones [PIC 2] with the gaps filled in with bricks hewn out of stone. Not mud-brick.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Dad found a snake skin about 5 feet long! [PIC 3] Which is higher than me. Mum saw a fat lizard.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went on to Rawlpindi. There was an escorted cart. The escorts were cavalry; their hats were a kind of turban with a shako on the top [PIC 4]. Then we went to the Army museum; there were some nice suits of chainmail.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We stayed all morning at Taxila and visited Jandial which no-one knows what it is really. At Sirkap, we saw some curved walls with some rooms that were the basis of bastions. F and I went back to fetch the camera, meanwhile Dad found a small dried snake skin and a huge one more that was as long as 5 feet.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We drove to Rawalpindi and visited the Army Museum. I liked the tanks, jeep and chainmail for a horse. We also saw a cavalry escort. We drove to Islamabad and camped at a campsite.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove round Islamabad, we saw lots of new Embassies. Then we went back to Raul-Pindi to get the cooking gas, then we drove to Lahore.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 37884 (10284 miles travelled). Lahore

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We entered Lahore just after lunchtime. We went to visit the Museum, near the Museum was a big Gun (Cannon) called Zamzama, it was very old. In the Museum, were some interesting little scenes with figures etc made of clay, there were rice grinders, a pottery factory and lacquer workshop, as well as Hindu and Muslim Marriage processions etc, and people on the streets. There were some beautiful Chinese things as well, in one of the rooms, I saw some Mascara jars, none as nice as mine though. Helena and I saw some little camel-bone cocktail sticks, with two elephants carved on one end, they were only 1 rupee (7p) each. Some of the goats are really enormous, and the sheep have really long ears, some even 1 foot long!

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We joined the Grand Trunk Road. It had some big bridges where river floods came down. There is a big flat plain, and as the road was on an embankment you could see a long wall. All the ground was either ploughed or something was growing. There were lots of big buffaloes with humps and horns. The horns spiralled inwards. The animals were very thin and you could see their bones. [PIC]

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We stayed at the Salvation Army. There is a really fat lady, who we think is American, who seems to be the chief, the loos are quite reasonable. In the morning we all had showers, there was no hot water brrr! We also did lots of washing clothes etc. We walked round the bazaar, H & I looked at lots of Bangles, I saw some new Mascara jars which looked as though they were being sold with Mascara. We bought some Tikkas (very small, unfortunately) and some Chapatties (bread). We had lunch in the park then drove to the Shalimar Gardens. (Shalimar had the Tahj-Mahal built as well) it was very beautiful with lots of green parrots and chipmunks.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We had gruel. It was rather thin but I liked it. We played Oliver [the musical]. Then we went to the bazaar, there were lots of bangles; some were glass, and had lovely colours that mixed and twisted beautifully. We got some food and had lunch.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Then we went to some gardens; they had some nice green parrots and chipmunks. The chipmunks had lovely bushy grey tails and white stripes. They were very fast runners. Helena and I watched them. They ate on the trees by hanging with their back legs and the food with the front. [PIC]

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: Shalimar Gardens. For breakfast, we had gruel (which F and I liked). After breakfast, we glued matches together to make stable walls. In the afternoon, we all visited a Bazaar. I only liked the bangles and embroidered tops. Soon we went to some very famous gardens where there were lots of chipmunks in the trees. The chipmunks had two brown stripes, a white belly and a very bushy tail and fur all over. They could run very fast.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We arrived at Lahore and drove straight to the Tourist Information. When Mum, Dad and D came back, we drove to the Museum where there were some clay models of weavers, potters, rice grinders, untouchables, and others who I did not look at. To get to Lahore, we joined the grand trunk road. On the grand trunk road there were lots of bulls, cows and horses pulling carts. Also there were lots and lots of lorries and buses.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 38032 (10432 miles travelled). Lahore

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We got up fairly early and went to see the big Mosque, supposed to be the biggest in the world, built by the last of the great Moghuls. Unlike the Persian Mosques, which had styles, it was lots of carved Marble etc. We went round the ‘Kashmir’ Bazaar, actually, it was all copper and things, across the road was thge jewellery bazaar, it had some beautiful gold bracelets etc.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to a big mosque. The courtyards were very [sic]. We went to the copper bazaar. There were lots of small models of Zamzam, the big cannon near the museum. Helena bought a tray, jug and goblet.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We did a speedy getaway and went to the Mosque. F and I did a hard poo then we climbed a minaret 1075 feet high. There were two balconies on the minaret. We walked through two courtyards - one with a garden and one just concrete.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Out of Pakistan. No P.R. left!

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Visited Golden Temple, Amritsar.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove to the border, getting into India was very tedious. I cooked some tortellini. India didn’t seem much different, but most of the guards were Sikhs, and had very nice, tidy turbans on. We drove to Amritsar, which is the centre of the Sikh religion there. We visited the Golden Temple, in its big pool. It was very impressive but I didn’t like the architecture.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We arrived at Amritsar and went to the Golden Temple of the Sikhs. They fed thousands of people every day. In the middle of a pool was a smaller temple. It was plated with gold. Inside there were some lovely paintings of animals; the animals were all biting each other.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We arrived at Amritsar, found a youth hostel and went to the golden temple (Temple of the Sikhs). There was a big tank of water.
